title: Experiment in training, not right after dying
summary: Sensitivity changes can be useful during deliberate practice, but changing it reactively during matches usually steals attention from the game and hides the real weakness.
why: Reactive mid-match setup changes often shift focus onto whether the sensitivity feels wrong instead of onto the actual game problem.
If the sensitivity feels off in matches, that often points to a real weakness that needs isolated practice rather than emotional setup hopping.
actions: Keep the match sensitivity stable during actual games so attention stays on decisions, clearing, and execution.
Write down the specific weakness you felt instead of changing sens on the spot.
Test alternate sensitivities later in deliberate practice blocks where you can isolate the issue calmly.
avoid: Do not tilt-change sensitivity right after deaths, missed shots, or bad rounds.
Avoid treating a sens swap as a substitute for targeted practice.

drills.label: Post-match weakness audit
drills.reason: A short review after matches preserves the useful signal without turning the game itself into setup experimentation.

evidence.claim: Sensitivity should be changed often in training with purpose, but kept stable during real matches to preserve focus on the game itself.
evidence.excerpt: The recommended split is deliberate experimentation in training and setup stability in actual matches.
